title: Micro-particle Image Velocimetry for Velocity Profile Measurements of Micro Blood Flows
protocol: Create or purchase a microchannel for the experiment.
Fabricate the PDMS channel using soft lithography techniques.
Expose the PDMS channel and glass slides to oxygenated plasma treatment for 45 seconds.
Press the treated PDMS channel firmly onto the glass slide to create a permanent bond.
Collect blood samples from an accredited facility.
Add 1 g of EDTA to 4 ml of water.
Mix the EDTA solution with 1 L of whole blood gently, repeating the process 10 times.
Allow the collected blood samples to cool slowly to room temperature.
Centrifuge the blood samples 3x at 3,000 rpm for 10 min each time.
Remove and discard plasma and buffy coat after the first centrifugation.
Add about 20 ml of phosphate buffered saline (PBS) and mix gently.
Recentrifuge the sample after adding PBS.
Remove and discard the PBS and remaining buffy coat after the third centrifugation.
Add fluorescing tracer particles at the desired concentration to blood samples.
Calibrate the system using a Newtonian solution before taking data.
Mix 30 μl of particles with 1 ml of blood solution for visualization in microcirculation.
Alternatively, use glycerol diluted with distilled water to a viscosity of 3cP as a calibration solution.
Close the laser curtain or turn on the laser sign on the lab door to prevent unauthorized access.
Use the shortest amount of tubing and the smallest rigid syringe possible.
Seal the tubing to the syringe and to the chip with glue, PDMS or Vaseline.
Remove the micro-syringe plunger.
Push liquid using a secondary plastic syringe attached to the channel's outlet.
Let liquid flow out until all microbubbles are removed from the system.
Replace the micro-syringe plunger.
Unplug the plastic syringe.
Verify the presence or absence of microbubbles with a microscope.
Level the syringe pump to achieve horizontal tubing.
Program the syringe pump to desired flow rate.
Place microchip on microscope stage.
Start the pump.
Use water with particles to calibrate the system to the middle velocity profile.
Calibrate the dT (the time between pulsed images).
Measure in the middle of the channel when calibrating.
Ensure particles move between 5 and 10 pixels between frames for good correlation.
Be careful of shadowing effects if using a round channel.
Fill syringe with desired quantity of blood.
Program the syringe pump to the desired flow rate.
Take desired data.
Refill the syringe every run or every other run to reduce RBC sedimentation.
Perform cross correlation on image pairs to obtain velocity vector fields.
Pre-process images to remove background noise before correlating.
Vary window sizes and shapes between adjacent images during cross correlation as needed.
Post-process images after cross correlation to remove erroneous vectors or outliers.
Shut down the system in a safe manner when measurements have been completed.
Use proper laser safety procedures until laser power source is completely shut down.
